column2: On the authority of al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Righteousness is good character, and sin is what wavers in your breast and you dislike people coming to know of it.” Reported by Muslim.
And on the authority of Wābiṣah ibn Maʿbad (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: “I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he said: You have come to ask about righteousness?

I said: Yes. He said: Righteousness is that with which the soul is at peace and the heart is at peace, and sin is what wavers in the soul and goes back and forth in the breast, even if people give you a ruling and give you rulings again.”
A ḥasan hadith; we have narrated it from the Musnads of the two imams Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and al-Dārimī with a ḥasan chain.

Al-birr (“righteousness”): Allah the Exalted explained it in His saying: “Righteousness is not that you turn your faces towards the east or the west; but righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book and the prophets; gives wealth, despite love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveller, those who ask, and for freeing slaves; establishes the prayer and gives the zakāh; [those who] fulfil their promise when they promise; and [those who] are patient in poverty and hardship and during battle. Those are the ones who have been true, and it is those who are the righteous” [al-Baqarah 2:177]. It has also been said:

it is what a person does of the obligatory and the recommended. Al-ithm (“sin”): wrongdoing. “What wavers in your breast”: what stirs in your soul and goes back and forth in your heart. “And you dislike”: with a religious dislike, “people coming to know of it”: the people of knowledge and religion.
Encouragement to good character.
Truth and falsehood are not confused for the discerning believer.
A ruling does not remove the doubt if the one seeking it is someone whose breast Allah has opened with the light of faith.
One seeking a ruling should seek it from someone more knowledgeable than himself and more fearful of Allah.
The miracle of the Messenger ﷺ in telling Wābiṣah what was in his mind before he spoke of it.
A person should not venture upon anything his soul is not at peace with.

In these two hadiths the Prophet ﷺ tells us that righteousness lies in good character, and that the best of people are those best in character, because of the general benefits in good character for every individual

and society, young and old, male and female. Part of good character is being kind to people, refraining from harming them, being at ease with them with gentle words, bearing their harm patiently, gentleness of speech with everyone, forbearance and not becoming angry;

that righteousness is that in which the heart and soul find rest; and that sin has two signs. The first is what wavers in your breast and goes back and forth in your soul, your heart not being at peace with its lawfulness or with going ahead and doing it. The second is that you dislike that

your doing this sin should be seen and become known, for fear of being blamed and censured for doing it and for believing it lawful. Even if the scholars give you a ruling, do not take their ruling as long as the sign of doubt keeps wavering in your soul, for a ruling does not remove the doubt as long as the doubt is genuine. Among what has been said about good character:
Adorn yourself with noble character, / so that the musk of your praise may spread its sweet fragrance.
Benefit your friend if you want his friendship, / and repel your enemy with that which [is better], and then the one who…

At the end of the verse he alludes to the saying of the Exalted: “And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] with that which is better; and then the one between you and whom there was enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend. But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one having a great portion [of good]” [Fuṣṣilat 41:34–35].
It has been said that good character is summed up in three phrases in the saying of the Exalted: “Take what is given freely, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant” [al-Aʿrāf 7:199].
